title: Forbes Riley's Elevator Pitch System for Cold Introductions
summary: Forbes Riley shares her step-by-step elevator pitch framework built on research, strategy, and leverage. She illustrates the process by describing how she pitched Grant Cardone through his wife Elena in 30 seconds.
key_points: Build cold pitches on three core pillars: Research, Strategy, and Leverage.
Prepare a clear pitch formula in advance to avoid freezing or rambling under pressure.
When approaching a target accompanied by a spouse or partner, approach the partner first with respect rather than walking directly up to the spouse.

Pitch example to the spouse: "Elena, hi. You may recognize me, Forbes Riley. I've been on television, $2.5 billion in sales. I make people billionaires. I think through an infomercial your husband could earn an extra billion. Would that be okay?"
Limit pitches for busy executives to 20–30 seconds.
Establish immediate authority by citing shared contacts (e.g., Kevin Harrington) and concise, high-impact numbers ($2.5 billion in sales).
Focus the pitch entirely on the prospect's desired outcome (e.g., earning an extra billion dollars) rather than just listing personal credentials.
content:
Post text:
If Elon Musk was standing in an elevator with you right now, what would you say? 👀

Most people would freeze, stumble or word vomit their entire life story in 10 seconds.

This week I sat down with bestselling author, TV host, and pitch expert Forbes Riley (@forbes_riley), and she broke down the real-life pitch that landed her on Grant Cardone's 10X stage.

Forbes was in a Vegas hallway. Grant was at the other end with his entire entourage. She had no meeting. No introduction. Just 20 seconds and a strategy.

She didn't approach Grant. She approached Elena.

And 30 seconds. That's all it took her to pitch herself 

Here's Forbes' framework so you're ready when YOUR elevator moment happens:

✅ Have your pitch ready BEFORE you need it. 

Forbes created a step-by-step elevator pitch system because she used to freeze and ramble in those moments. Prepare now so you can perform later. 

✅ Do your research obsessively. 

Forbes already knew Grant's net worth, and who Elena was and that 30-second pitch had hours of research behind it. 

✅ Don't pitch the gatekeeper. Win them over. 

Forbes approached Elena with respect and a clear value proposition. The door opened because she read the room, not because she forced her way in. 

✅ Make the pitch about THEIR outcome. 

"I can make you an extra billion" is about Grant's result. Not Forbes' resume. Flip every pitch from "here's what I've done" to "here's what I'll do for YOU."

The opportunities you want are one bold conversation away. But only if you're prepared for the moment. 💯

Follow me @yapwithhala, then comment FORBES and I'll send you the full episode 🔗

Make a note of this post.

Transcript:
Hala Taha: If somebody that you want to meet is in the elevator with you, let's put Elon Musk in the elevator. What do you say to him?
Forbes Riley: I have a thing called elevator pitch. I would get very nervous when I would meet new people and throw up on them. So I created this elevator pitch, and it's a very step-by-step system to allow people who are shy or introverted or just confused about how to position themselves to say hi. And so, I had heard about Grant Cardone, and I heard he was going to be in Vegas. I was there, and I tracked him down. I'm in a hallway, and I see him at the very end of the hallway with a whole entourage. Now I've got 20 seconds to put something together. 1, I believe in research. 2, I believe in strategy, and 3, I believe in leverage. Those are my three key core pillars. And so as I walked up to Grant, my thought was when one woman walks up to somebody else's husband, because I knew who Elena was by my research, don't walk up to the husband because it's not a good energy. And so I walked right up to her. And I said, "Elena, hi. You may recognize me, Forbes Riley. I've been on television, $2.5 billion in sales. I make people billionaires. I think through an infomercial your husband could earn an extra billion. Would that be okay?" She turns to Grant and says, "You need to meet this woman." She literally opened the door. Now, for busy men, you get 20 seconds, and I know that's how his brain works. I'm like, "Hey Grant, nice to meet you. I'm friends with Kevin Harrington"—I dropped a name that we both know very well. I said, "I've generated over two and a half billion. I'd like to see if I can make you an extra billion." I already know he's a billionaire, so that's credibility and authority and loving on him, doing an infomercial. He looked at me, he said, "Great. I'm doing a party in two nights. You're my special guest." The whole thing was maybe 30 seconds. And then he invited me on his 10X stage.
